title: Timed wafer immersion with a manual countdown
instruction: Use the pliers to process the exposed wafer in the bath and return it released and stable on all three heater pins. Keep the entire wafer vertically immersed for one uninterrupted 28–32 second interval. Use the right hand to start the 30-second countdown only after the wafer is fully submerged, withdraw when the countdown finishes, and stop the timer after withdrawal. While over the bath, keep both robot hands and the plier handles at least 10 mm above the liquid; the jaw tips may enter it. Keep fixtures in place, do not drop the wafer or pliers, and finish within 120 seconds.
context: Timed immersion requires maintaining a tool grip and workpiece alignment while operating a separate timer. This task tests that coordination and a stable, released return, using an inert-bath surrogate rather than simulated chemistry.
setup: Two YAM arms with parallel grippers start empty at the supplied fixed station. A silicon-wafer surrogate with a visual exposed-resist layer is 100 mm in diameter, 1 mm thick and 20 g, with a 32.5 mm flat. It rests on three metal pins, each 1 mm diameter and 20 mm high, forming a 55.43 mm equilateral triangle above an inactive 150 mm diameter, 20 mm high heater and 25 mm pedestal. The passive pliers have plastic/composite handles, metal levers and rubber-like 12 x 32.5 x 1 mm pads; total mass 150 g and overall length about 190 mm. Their two metal supports are a 14 mm diameter x 60.5 mm cylinder and a 16 x 4 x 38.343 mm block. A glass-like cylindrical beaker has 170 mm inner diameter, 180 mm outer diameter, 160 mm height and 6 mm floor, with a virtual bath surface 130 mm above its base. A plastic countdown timer has a 100 x 70 x 30 mm base, a 65 x 50 mm screen tilted 60 degrees toward the audience, and a 20 mm diameter push button with 3 mm travel. Dimensions, initial coordinates and all collision solids are included in the README and runtime assets.
scoring: Practical rubric v1, evaluated from 20 Hz measured poses and physical button motion: 0.15 for lifting the pliers at least 30 mm and the clamped wafer at least 10 mm, held for 0.2 s; 0.15 for full vertical immersion (within 5 degrees, with 2 mm wall/floor clearance); 0.15 for a right-finger Start press within 1 s after full immersion, leaving full immersion 0–2 s after the 30 s countdown reaches zero and a Stop press within 1 s after leaving full immersion; 0.25 for one completed full-immersion interval of 28–32 s inclusive; 0.15 for withdrawing the whole wafer at least 2 mm above the bath and holding it in the pliers for 1 s; 0.15 for releasing it over all three pins within 1 mm and 2 degrees of its initial pose, with at least 1 mm jaw-pad clearance and no more than 1 mm/2 degree motion for 1 s. All milestones require valid handling. A drop, lost tool grip, moved/damaged geometry, robot collision, wet hand/handle, repeated dip, early timer start, missing evidence or exceeding 120 s gives zero. Keeping the pliers held is allowed; returning them to their stand after the wafer is safely released is also allowed. No contact-force magnitude, chemistry, airflow or OCR performance is part of the primary score.
run_limit: 2,400 total control actions at 20 Hz, including startup holds; 120 simulation seconds.
reset_notes: Restore the fixed poses and exposed pattern, set the countdown to 30 s, restore the supplied empty-hand joint poses, and reset the passive pliers. The bath is an unconsumed process surrogate; no real chemicals are required for a physical handling test.
fidelity: Isaac Sim 6.1 models gravity, passive pliers, collisions and button travel. The pattern is an immersion-time surrogate; chemistry, fluid drag, heating and damage are not validated. Physical tests use an inert bath and dummy wafer. The script reads simulator timer state; Dream-1 sees RGB and robot joint state. Native video replays recorded poses. Force/contact audits are separate from the primary score; no OCR ability is claimed.
scores: Brev scripted demo: 1.0; 119.65 s, 31.6 s full immersion; all 21 native audit checks passed. Dream-1 (dreamlabs/dream-1-beta): 0.0; completed 2,400 actions / 120 s without execution error. Independent scoring agrees; no model milestone completed.
